lessons.claim: A de-duplication pass spawns duplicates while it runs, and both directions happened on 2026-08-29: a peer session fixing a table-divergence bug added a FOURTH copy of the water viscosity table inside its verifier, and a test written to assert that two packages share one table copied three handbook rows into its own body. The distinction that makes a copy legitimate is not intent, it is whether the copy is (a) labelled as a frozen pre-merge snapshot, (b) read by nothing but the comparison, and (c) wrong-by-construction if anyone updates it -- a bit-identity verifier MUST hold its own copy, since you cannot prove a move changed nothing by importing the thing you moved. Everything else should read the single source. Before finishing a dedup pass, grep the tree for the literals you just centralised, including in the tests and verifiers you added during the pass.
